attacks.claim: If the cursor row is no longer in the user's saved list (unsaved or deleted between page requests), findIndex returns -1, so start becomes 0 and the endpoint silently returns the first page again instead of an error or a resumable position. A client following nextCursor can then loop or show duplicates.
attacks.evidence: const start = cursor ? rows.findIndex((r) => r.id === cursor) + 1 : 0;
